scope: Four units independently reviewed: three caption-link repair scenes and the newly identified workflow-second-channel/two-channels scene. Eight unaffected units carry source12 ratings by exact compiled feature metadata; two LFO units carry source13 ratings on identical book/index pins. This report does not claim a fresh review of all reader units.

fresh_units.title: Select Oilcan 1
fresh_units.focus: Oilcan 1 as a draft on channel 1 for percussion

caption_link.text: Apply Oilcan to the percussion channel

coherence.rationale: The selected frame labels Oilcan 1 as a draft on channel 1; its caption says K3 applies it and the Apply sequence ends with the value still present and no prompt.

usefulness.rationale: The reader gives the device install/enable setup, E3 selection, K3 confirmation, and a re-open check; the four-frame Apply route includes all four actions.

understandability.rationale: The displayed caption separates draft selection from the confirmation action, and the final frame explicitly says the prompt is gone.

representation.rationale: All three owner routes and all three explicit-step routes show the Oilcan frame and a visible caption anchor; the reader also presents its recorded norns screen and grid.

granularity.rationale: The selection remains a single focused captured frame, while the separate Apply destination carries the four-step confirm-and-reopen procedure.

flow.rationale: Clicking the caption moves from the draft scene to “Apply Oilcan to the percussion channel,” whose sequence progresses from opening Device through K3 confirmation to reopening it.

integration.rationale: The caption link resolves to its authored Apply target on click, and the three owner routes plus their explicit-step routes all render the same intended selection.

vocabulary.rationale: Device, channel, draft, E3, and K3 match the shown controls and action; “n.b. mod” remains domain-specific terminology.

naming.rationale: “Select Oilcan 1” names the chosen player, while the destination names the percussion channel and the apply task.

canonical_home.rationale: The caption opens the canonical Oilcan Apply route, and all three owner placements plus all three explicit-step paths resolve to the same selected-player state.

representation.rationale: The visible caption anchor works on all three owner routes and all three explicit-step routes; the recorded screen/grid and four-step Apply viewer are visible.

granularity.rationale: The selection frame stays focused, with the longer K3 Apply-and-reopen sequence in a separate captured scene.

flow.rationale: The caption handoff opens the matching chord-channel Apply route; its steps proceed from Device through selecting, confirming, and reopening.

integration.rationale: The actual caption click reaches the authored Doubledecker Apply route, and each of the six owner/step routes shows the same selection and link.

vocabulary.rationale: The channel, Device, draft, E3 and K3 wording matches the displayed controls; “n.b. mod” is the main specialized term.

naming.rationale: The title identifies Doubledecker; the caption destination names the chord channel and Apply task.

canonical_home.rationale: The caption opens the canonical Doubledecker Apply route, while all three owner placements and all three explicit-step paths load the intended selection.

fresh_units.title: Add one keyboard note and check both channel outputs
fresh_units.focus: Add MIDI note 76 to step 3 on channel 2 while checking separate channel 1 and channel 2 routes

coherence.rationale: The final checkpoint says to add note 76 to channel 2 step 3 and check the original channel 1 phrase plus the new channel 2 note; the captured state is the matching Note Masks checkpoint.

usefulness.rationale: It supplies an actionable note, velocity, step, channel, transport check, and expected MIDI values/routes for both outputs.

understandability.rationale: The starting point explains that a port is an output and a channel is its numbered route; the precise MIDI list is useful but dense.

representation.rationale: The five-step recorded scene shows the norns screen, full grid, final caption, and the newly rendered “MIDI Keyboard Input” anchor.

granularity.rationale: The current two-channel checkpoint is one step within a five-frame workflow; the caption is long because it retains both expected output sequences.

flow.rationale: The last checkpoint links back to the feature route for the complete workflow; the click lands on the MIDI Keyboard Input page with its full lesson context.

integration.rationale: The contextual link is visible and clickable from the nested current placement, and its destination resolves to the owning MIDI Keyboard Input route.

vocabulary.rationale: Mask, step, velocity, port and channel are used consistently, with the starting-point text defining port and channel; the notation assumes basic MIDI familiarity.

naming.rationale: The parent title names MIDI Keyboard Input and the checkpoint names the two channel outputs being checked.

canonical_home.rationale: The caption’s explicit route opens the canonical MIDI Keyboard Input owner route and shows its complete lesson context.

method: Cold full-document navigations checked all nine bare owner placements and all nine explicit select-player placements for the three player scenes. Each route was matched against the expected player title and loaded caption anchor href. Each caption anchor was clicked and the destination was checked. The three Apply sequences were inspected through their reader controls (four captured Oilcan and Doubledecker steps; Polyperc Show result); no native application was run, and no audio was played or listened to. The workflow two-channels route was loaded, its MIDI Keyboard Input caption anchor clicked, and the destination checked. The old start-card wording is in the DOM but computed display:none and zero-sized, so it was excluded from ratings.
